test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: As per the June 2025 India Child Protection report, what percentage of 44,902 rescued children were found in the worst forms of child labour?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.9%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **June 2025 India Child Protection report** highlighted the alarming situation of child labour in India.
 
• A total of **44,902 children** were rescued during the reporting period under child protection initiatives.
 
• Out of these rescued children, **0.9% were found in the worst forms of child labour**, which include hazardous industries, bonded labour, and child trafficking for labour exploitation.
 
• The term "worst forms of child labour" is defined under the **International Labour Organization (ILO) Convention No. 182**, which India ratified in **2017**. It includes activities that are hazardous or exploitative for children.
 
• The correct percentage is **0.9%**, which signifies the proportion of children engaged in these severe forms of exploitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Child Labour:**

 
 
• The term "child labour" refers to the employment of children in any work that deprives them of their childhood, interferes with their ability to attend school, and is mentally, physically, socially, or morally harmful.
 
• It is defined in the **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986** in India.
 
 
 
• **Worst Forms of Child Labour:**
 
 
• Activities categorized under "worst forms" include **slavery or practices similar to slavery**, such as debt bondage, forced labour, and trafficking.
 
• Engagement in hazardous industries like mining, construction, and chemical production also falls under this category.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework in India:**
 
 
• The **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016** prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in any form of labour and adolescents (14-18 years) in hazardous occupations.
 
• The **Right to Education Act, 2009** ensures free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years, addressing one of the root causes of child labour.
 
 
 
• **International Efforts:**
 
 
• The **ILO's International Programme on the Elimination of Child Labour (IPEC)** aims to eliminate child labour globally.
 
• India ratified the **ILO Convention No. 138** (Minimum Age Convention) and **No. 182** (Worst Forms of Child Labour Convention) in 2017, committing to abolishing child labour.
 
 
 
• **Important Statistics:**
 
 
• According to the **2021 UNICEF report**, approximately **160 million children** globally are engaged in child labour, with a significant proportion in hazardous work.
 
• In India, the **Census 2011** reported over **10 million children** engaged in child labour, though recent initiatives have significantly reduced this number.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Initiatives in India:**

 
 
• The **National Child Labour Project (NCLP)** scheme rehabilitates children withdrawn from child labour and provides them with education and vocational training.
 
• The **PENCIL portal** (Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour) was launched in 2017 to ensure effective enforcement of child labour laws.
 
 
 
• **Role of NGOs:**
 
 
• Organizations like **Bachpan Bachao Andolan** and **Child Rights and You (CRY)** have been instrumental in rescuing children and spreading awareness about child labour.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Eradicating Child Labour:**
 
 
• Poverty, lack of education, and social norms continue to drive child labour in India and globally.
 
• Effective enforcement of laws and rehabilitation of rescued children remain significant challenges.
